title: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)

sections.label: MRT network expansion plans
sections.summary: Seven TEL stations and a NEL extension to Punggol Coast will bring almost 150 stations across six MRT lines, with another 100 kilometres added to the 258-kilometre network in about 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the expected opening of seven Thomson East Coast Line (TEL) stations and a North East Line (NEL) extension to Punggol Coast this year, that will take us to almost 150 stations across six Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) lines across our island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Yet, we are still expecting to add another 100 kilometres to our 258-kilometre long rail network in the next 10 years or so.

sections.label: Deferred 15.6% fare increase
sections.summary: The Public Transport Council deferred a 15.6% fare increase for future fare review exercises, made possible by an additional $300 million in Government subsidies in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Causing some concern is the 15.6% fare increase that was deferred by the Public Transport Council (PTC) for future fare review exercises, meaning similar fare hikes may be expected in the subsequent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The deferment of the 15.6% fare increase was only made possible by the Government's provision of an additional $300 million in subsidies in 2024 to make up the funding gap.

sections.label: Growth of rail network
sections.summary: The rail network is set to grow with at least 50 new train stations and several new interchanges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Our rail network is poised to grow significantly in the coming years, with the addition of at least 50 new train stations and several new interchanges.

sections.label: Barrier-free transport facilities
sections.summary: All MRT and LRT stations are barrier-free, all bus interchanges and 98% of bus shelters are barrier-free, all public buses are wheelchair accessible, and most bus interchanges have baby care rooms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Most stations and buses are equipped with facilities such as ramps and elevators to facilitate easy access.” In fact, all MRT and LRT stations in Singapore are barrier-free; all bus interchanges and 98% of bus shelters in Singapore are barrier-free; all public buses are wheelchair accessible; and most bus interchanges have baby care rooms for families with young children.

sections.label: P2P transport satisfaction survey
sections.summary: A Public Transport Council survey showed overall improvement in satisfaction with P2P transport services, but concerns persist over the declining taxi population and rising P2P demand in a zero Vehicle Growth Rate environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The recent Public Transport Council survey revealed an overall improvement in satisfaction with P2P transport services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, concerns persist, particularly regarding to the decline in taxi population and the increasing demand for P2P services, especially in a zero Vehicle Growth Rate environment.

sections.label: PHC loans and COE category
sections.summary: PHC drivers can borrow 90% to 100% of a car's market value versus 60% to 70% for privately owned cars, raising concerns about more cars registered as private hire vehicles; MOT said a separate COE category for ride-hail cars was not ruled out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: As private hire car (PHC) drivers can borrow up to 90% to 100% of the car’s market value compared to 60% to 70% for privately owned cars, there are concerns that more car buyers are registering their cars as private hire vehicles, so that they can secure higher loan amounts in order to afford them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: In January this year, MOT shared that the Government would not rule out the creation of a new separate COE category for ride-hail cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Would the Minister share an update on its study on this issue?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: We need to cap our roughly one million vehicle population in light of Singapore’s constraints in land and carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: This has resulted in increasing COE prices, especially with rising incomes.

sections.label: Zero-growth rate policy for vehicles
sections.summary: The zero-growth rate policy for cars and motorcycles was implemented in 2018 and continues until 31 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In order to temper vehicle population growth, the zero-growth rate policy for car and motorcycles was implemented in 2018, and will continue until next year, 31 January 2025.

sections.label: Zero-growth policy beyond January 2025
sections.summary: The question asks whether MOT intends to continue the zero-growth rate policy beyond January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Does MOT intend to continue the zero-growth rate policy beyond January 2025?

sections.label: Take-up rates of vehicle types
sections.summary: The question asks for 2023 take-up rates of EVs, hybrid vehicles and ICE vehicles in new private car sales.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For new private car sales in 2023, what were the take-up rates of EVs, hybrid vehicles and ICE vehicles respectively?

sections.label: Sufficiency of EV charging points
sections.summary: The question asks whether the sufficiency of EV charging points within the constituency can be predicted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Are we able to predict the sufficiency of EV charging points within the constituency?

sections.label: Faster EV charging times
sections.summary: The question asks whether MOT can introduce chargers that charge an EV in less than the current four to five hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Would the MOT be able to introduce chargers that can charge the EV within a shorter period of time, instead of the current four to five hours?

sections.label: Friendly Street and road safety
sections.summary: The passage welcomes Friendly Street and asks whether it has made roads safer and whether LTA will educate pedestrians more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I receive many complains too, that there are drivers who do not use their signal indicators, thus, causing near accidents, because the rear driver does not know that the front driver intends to make a turn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, I welcome the introduction of "Friendly Street", announced by LTA last December, because this signals to the public that road safety is important for all residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But I wish to find out more whether the introduction of Friendly Street, has it actually resulted in safer roads for road users?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Would LTA do more to educate pedestrians to be more mindful of the need for road safety?

sections.label: Traffic accident deaths increase
sections.summary: Traffic accidents killed 136 people in 2023, a 25.9% rise from 108 deaths in 2022, with more fatal accidents involving speeding, red lights and drink driving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Traffic accidents claimed the lives of 136 people in 2023, which is a 25.9% increase from the 108 deaths in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We also saw an increase in the number of fatal accidents involving speeding, running red lights and drink driving.

sections.label: Vulnerable road user groups
sections.summary: Motorcyclists and pillion riders make up nearly half of last year's fatalities and the elderly 20%, with LTA rolling out more Silver Zones for the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our vulnerable road user groups include motorcyclists and their pillion riders, who make up nearly half of all fatalities last year, and the elderly, who account for 20% of fatalities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For our elderly, LTA is already rolling out more Silver Zones, which have lower speed limits and other traffic-calming measures.

sections.label: Friendly Streets Pilot learning points
sections.summary: The question asks the Ministry for an update on learning points from the earlier Friendly Streets Pilot in Ang Mo Kio, Bukit Batok West, Tampines, Toa Payoh and West Coast.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Can the Ministry give an update to the learning points gleamed from the earlier Friendly Streets Pilot in Ang Mo Kio, Bukit Batok West, Tampines, Toa Payoh and West Coast?

sections.label: Covered walkway construction focus
sections.summary: LTA focuses on covered walkways within 400 metres of MRT stations and 200 metres of bus interchanges and limited bus stops, neglecting other major bus stops linked to essential amenities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Chairman, currently, LTA solely focuses on constructing covered walkways within a 400-metre radius of MRT stations, and a 200-metre radius of bus interchanges and limited number of bus stops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: However, this approach neglects many other major bus stops that are linked to town centres, markets, hawker centres, polyclinics and other essential amenities that are not situated near MRT stations or bus interchanges.

sections.label: PMA medical certification and speed limits
sections.summary: The member supports AMAP's December 2023 recommendations to impose medical certification requirements and speed limitation on PMAs, and asks the Ministry for the implementation timeframe.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Such errant and selfish behaviour threatens the safety of fellow walkway users, especially seniors and young children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Hence, I fully support the recommendations tabled by the Active Mobility Advisory Panel (AMAP) in December 2023 to impose medical certification requirements and speed limitation on PMAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share the timeframe to implement these recommendations?

sections.label: Clearer PMA regulations
sections.summary: The question asks whether LTA would consider clearer regulations on PMA use before the situation deteriorates and the PMD problem repeats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: Would LTA consider having clearer regulations regarding the use of PMAs before the situation deteriorates and then we would face the same problem that we had with PMDs.

sections.label: PMA speed limit and medical certification
sections.summary: AMAP recommended a six kilometres per hour speed limit for PMAs like mobility scooters and medical certification for users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In the recent review of existing regulations for PMAs, such as mobility scooters, AMAP recommended a speed limit of six kilometres per hour and for users to be medically certified.

sections.label: Mobility scooter user eligibility
sections.summary: AMAP recommended allowing only users certified to have medical needs or walking difficulties to use mobility scooters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: AMAP has recommended to allow only users who are certified to have medical needs or walking difficulties to use mobility scooters.

sections.label: Income losses and transitionary measures
sections.summary: The question asks whether studies were done on income losses for affected riders and whether transitionary measures including trade-in arrangements will be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Has studies been done on the potential income losses for this affected group of riders?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider some transitionary measures, including trade-in arrangements for non-compliant devices?

sections.label: Lowering PMA speed limit
sections.summary: AMAP recommended lowering the speed limit of all motorised PMAs from 10 to six kilometres per hour and restricting sales to authorised retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: In December last year, AMAP recommended lowering the speed limit of all motorised PMAs from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour and only allowing authorised retailers to sell PMAs with a maximum device speed of no more than six kilometres per hour.

sections.label: Singapore maritime sector milestones
sections.summary: In 2023, Singapore's annual vessel arrival tonnage crossed three billion gross tonnage and container throughput reached 39 million TEUs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: In 2023, Singapore’s annual vessel arrival tonnage crossed the three billion gross tonnage milestone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Our container throughput also reached a new high of 39 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs).

sections.label: Tuas Mega Port construction progress
sections.summary: The passage states Tuas Mega Port will be the world's largest fully automated port, with Phase 1 started in September 2022 and workers expected to double.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: The continued growth in our maritime sector will be underpinned by the construction of the Tuas Mega Port, which will be the world’s largest fully automated port when it is completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Are we on track for the target completion date?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: We started Phase 1 of port operations at Tuas in September 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Today, we have some 800 workers working there and this is expected to double to about 1,600 workers by the end of this year.

sections.label: New harbour craft fuel requirements
sections.summary: From 2030, all new harbour craft in Singapore's port waters must be fully electric, use B100 biofuels, or be compatible with net-zero fuels like hydrogen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To achieve this transition, from 2030, all new harbour craft operating in Singapore's port waters will be required to be fully electric, capable of using B100 biofuels, or compatible with net-zero fuels, such as hydrogen.

sections.label: Record port and bunker sales
sections.summary: Singapore's port received a record 3.09 billion annual gross tons in vessel arrivals and handled a record number of shipping containers in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: At the same time, I am heartened to hear that our port received a record 3.09 billion annual gross tons in vessel arrivals and handled a record number of shipping containers in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The record vessel arrivals in 2023 has also helped us break the 2017 record for bunker sales, registering 51.82 million tons in 2023.

sections.label: New MRT and LRT stations
sections.summary: More than 50 stations will be added to the existing 200 MRT and LRT stations by 2030, requiring hundreds to thousands of new roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: As we look to add more than 50 stations to our existing 200 MRT and LRT stations by 2030, hundreds to thousands of new roles will need to be filled.

sections.label: Changi Airport traffic recovery
sections.summary: Changi Airport's passenger traffic, flights and city links stood at about 80% of pre-COVID-19 levels and were expected to return to pre-pandemic levels by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: On the aviation sector, we heard at last year's COS that Changi Airport's passenger traffic volumes, flights and city links stood at about 80% of pre-COVID-19 levels and were expected to return to pre-pandemic levels by 2024, if not earlier.

sections.label: Sustainable Aviation Fuel levy
sections.summary: From 2026, travellers flying out of Singapore must pay a levy to support greener jet fuel, with Sustainable Aviation Fuel targets for 2026 and 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: From 2026, travellers flying out of Singapore will need to pay a levy to support the use of greener jet fuel.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: MOT aims for Sustainable Aviation Fuel to constitute 1% of all jet fuel used at Changi Airport and Seletar Airport in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: The longer-term goal is for Sustainable Aviation Fuel to reach 3% to 5% by 2030 to help reduce Singapore's international aviation emissions by about 4%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Singapore is the first country in the world to impose a Sustainable Aviation Fuel levy on passengers.

sections.label: Singapore Aviation Academy upgrade
sections.summary: MOT announced a $120 million upgrade for the Singapore Aviation Academy, which will boost its training capacity by 20% when completed in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: MOT recently announced the $120 million upgrade for the Singapore Aviation Academy, which will boost its training capacity by 20% when it is completed in 2026.

sections.label: Walk-Cycle-Ride mode share
sections.summary: Forward SG participants agreed this direction suits land-scarce Singapore, and Walk-Cycle-Ride mode share rose from 71% in 2016 to 74% in 2022 while driving fell from 29% to 26%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: During the Forward SG exercise, many participants agreed this was the right direction to take in land-scarce Singapore, to meet our connectivity needs in a sustainable manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We have increased our Walk-Cycle-Ride mode share for peak period journeys, from 71% in 2016 to 74% in 2022, while the proportion who drove decreased from 29% to 26% over the same period.

sections.label: Marine Parade to Shenton Way travel time
sections.summary: TEL will cut Marine Parade to Shenton Way travel to 20 minutes from about 40, and commuters get free TEL4 preview rides on 21 June.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Travelling from Marine Parade to Shenton Way will take 20 minutes via TEL, compared to about 40 minutes today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Commuters can enjoy free rides on TEL4 during the preview on 21 June.

sections.label: Rail expansion stations and households
sections.summary: Expansion efforts up to 2026 add 16 stations, benefiting 90,000 more households in the east, northeast and central areas toward the 2030s target.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Altogether, these expansion efforts up to 2026 will add 16 stations to our rail network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Gan Thiam Poh's questions, these will benefit 90,000 more households across the east, northeast and central areas, bringing us closer to our target for eight in 10 households to be within a 10-minute walk of a train station by the 2030s.

sections.label: Rail reliability incentive and transport subsidies
sections.summary: From 2024 to 2028 the Government provides a Rail Reliability and Performance Incentive, plus over $2 billion yearly in public transport subsidies and additional subsidies of about $200 million and $300 million in 2023 and 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: From 2024 to 2028, the Government will provide a Rail Reliability and Performance Incentive to the operators to incentivise them to keep up rail reliability standards, invest in workers and improve manpower productivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Government currently provides over $2 billion of subsidies for public transport every year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To keep fares affordable for commuters, the Public Transport Council did not grant the maximum allowable fare increase in the past two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: So, the Government provided additional subsidies of about $200 million and $300 million in 2023 and 2024 respectively.

sections.label: Lower-income public transport spending share
sections.summary: Among lower-income households, public transport spending as a proportion of household income fell from 3.1% in 2013 to 2.4% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Among lower-income households, spending on public transport as a proportion of household income has reduced from 3.1% in 2013 to 2.4% in 2022.

sections.label: Panel recommendations for mobility devices
sections.summary: The panel recommended certifying mobility scooter users, cutting the speed limit from 10 to six kilometres per hour, and imposing size limits for PMAs on paths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The panel had recommended certifying those who want to use mobility scooters, reducing the speed limit from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour and imposing size limits for PMAs on paths.

sections.label: Sustainable Aviation Fuel targets
sections.summary: MOT set a 1% Sustainable Aviation Fuel uplift target from 2026, aiming for 3% to 5% by 2030, subject to global developments and wider availability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MOT announced a target of 1% Sustainable Aviation Fuels uplift in Singapore from 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our goal is to raise the Sustainable Aviation Fuel target beyond 1% in 2026 to between 3% and 5% by 2030, subject to global developments and the wider availability and adoption of Sustainable Aviation Fuel.

sections.label: MPA sustainability co-funding
sections.summary: MPA will set aside $15 million till 2030 to co-fund qualifying costs for pre-approved sustainability solutions, with 50% for SMEs and 30% for non-SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MPA will set aside $15 million till 2030 to co-fund qualifying costs for adopting pre-approved sustainability solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) can receive 50% co-funding, while non-SMEs can receive 30% co-funding, up to $30,000 per solution.

sections.label: EV share of new cars
sections.summary: In 2023, more than 18% of new cars registered were EVs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In 2023, more than 18% of new cars registered were EVs.

sections.label: Fast chargers installed
sections.summary: In total, 120 fast chargers will be installed at about 60 carparks under this initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In total, there will be 120 fast chargers installed at about 60 carparks under this initiative.

sections.label: Changi capacity expansion
sections.summary: Reopened Terminal 2 raised Changi's annual capacity to 90 million passengers, and T5 will add 50 million more in the mid-2030s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We reopened the expanded Terminal 2 in November last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This increased Changi’s annual capacity to 90 million passengers across all four terminals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: When completed in the mid-2030s, T5 will add another 50 million passengers to Changi’s annual capacity and further strengthen Singapore’s aviation connectivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Works have also resumed on the Changi East Industrial Zone, to be completed in the mid-2030s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This will double Singapore’s air cargo handling capacity from about three million tonnes per annum today to more than five million tonnes per annum.

sections.label: Logistics Alliance for Action
sections.summary: DB Schenker, PSA, Cargo Community Network, SATS, Singapore Airlines Cargo and the Singapore Aircargo Agents Association will form an Alliance for Action with MOT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: If we can do that, it will reduce time and cost for logistic providers and their customers, and importantly, we allow Singapore to differentiate ourselves from the competition as a trusted and efficient multi-modal logistics hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that DB Schenker, PSA, Cargo Community Network, SATS, Singapore Airlines Cargo and the Singapore Aircargo Agents Association have decided to come together to form an Alliance for Action (AfA), together with MOT, to co-develop solutions that can overcome the current bottlenecks and achieve our shared targets.

sections.label: Aviation Work-Study Diploma Intake
sections.summary: The Work-Study Diploma in Customer Experience Management in Aviation was launched, and aviation employers are expanding their intake of ITE Work-Study Diploma students to 90 this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Last year, we launched the Work-Study Diploma in Customer Experience Management in Aviation, adding to the 1,800 graduates from our aviation and aerospace-related programmes every year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Aviation employers like SATS and dnata continue expand their targeted intake of ITE Work-Study Diploma students to 90 this year, which is more than double that of 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In fact, about 40% of our 500 air traffic controllers are women.

sections.label: Land Transshipment Permit Streamlining
sections.summary: Land transshipment procedures will be streamlined so companies transshipping goods via land checkpoints need only one permit instead of two.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Coming back to supply chain connectivity, we will streamline land transshipment procedures so that instead of two permits – one for import and one for export – companies transshipping goods via land checkpoints will only require one permit.

sections.label: Estimated Industry Savings
sections.summary: Aggregated across the industry, potential savings of up to $2 million per year are estimated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Aggregated across the industry, we estimate potential savings of up to $2 million per year.

sections.label: Port 5G Coverage and Strengths
sections.summary: 5G coverage in port waters will be completed by mid-2025, and Singapore's key strengths include long-term planning, tripartite partnership and openness to investment, ideas and talent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In many other ports, they may find difficulty in implementing something like this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We are also going to complete the 5G coverage in our port waters by mid-2025 and this will allow more seamless provision of marine services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Singapore has some key strengths that allow us to achieve these aspirations: our ability to plan long-term and prepare ahead of time; our strong tripartite partnership with industry and unions that has been built on a high degree of trust over the years; and our openness to investment, to ideas, to talent from around the world to complement our Singapore core.

sections.label: Friendly Streets Additional Funding
sections.summary: As the Minister earlier announced, $1 billion of additional funding will be set aside to expand the Friendly Streets initiative and build more commuter infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As the Minister earlier announced, we will set aside $1 billion of additional funding to expand the Friendly Streets initiative and build more commuter infrastructure.

sections.label: Friendly Streets Expansion Engagements
sections.summary: The Friendly Streets initiative will expand to all HDB towns by 2030 and to private estates with high-activity areas and key amenities nearby, with engagements starting this year on 10 more Friendly Streets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Having sat in the taskforce meetings, I am heartened by the passion of stakeholders to create safer and more inclusive roads.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will expand the Friendly Streets initiative to all HDB towns by 2030, as well as to private estates with high-activity areas and key amenities nearby.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Starting this year, we will begin engagements on 10 more Friendly Streets in Bedok, Buangkok, Bukit Panjang, Choa Chu Kang, Jurong East, Pek Kio, Punggol, Holland/Buona Vista, Sembawang and Tiong Bahru/Havelock.

sections.label: Bus stop upgrades
sections.summary: Under LTA's Bus Stop Infrastructure Enhancement Programme, 255 bus stops were upgraded to be barrier-free and senior-friendly, with 105 more expected by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Under LTA’s Bus Stop Infrastructure Enhancement Programme, we have upgraded 255 bus stops to be barrier-free and senior-friendly, and expect to upgrade another 105 bus stops by 2025.

sections.label: Road repurposing projects
sections.summary: Works to pedestrianise Choa Chu Kang Terrace and Yung Sheng Road began in end-2023, and two new road repurposing projects at Zion Road and Sims Place start in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In end-2023, we started works to pedestrianise Choa Chu Kang Terrace and Yung Sheng Road.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will embark on two new road repurposing projects at Zion Road and Sims Place in 2024.

sections.label: Cycling path network expansion
sections.summary: The expansion of the cycling path network is on track to meet the target of 1,300 kilometres of cycling paths by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To enhance connectivity, we are pressing on with the expansion of our cycling path network.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We are on track to meet our target of 1,300 kilometres of cycling paths by 2030.

sections.label: Cycling paths in HDB towns
sections.summary: All 27 HDB towns and estates will have cycling paths by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: With that, all 27 HDB towns and estates will have cycling paths by the end of this year.

sections.label: PMA regulations recommendations accepted
sections.summary: The Government accepts AMAP's recommendations on PMA regulations, as earlier mentioned by the Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As earlier mentioned by the Minister, the Government accepts AMAP's recommendations on PMA regulations.

sections.label: PMA speed limit lowered
sections.summary: The speed limit of all PMAs will be lowered from 10 kilometres per hour to six km/h.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: First, the speed limit of all PMAs will be lowered from 10 kilometres per hour (km/h) to six km/h.

sections.label: PMA size and weight limits
sections.summary: PMAs on public paths should not exceed 70cm width, 120cm length, 150cm height and 300kg laden weight.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Going forward, PMAs used on public paths should not exceed a width of 70 centimetres, a length of 120 centimetres, a height of 150 centimetres and a laden weight of 300 kilograms.

sections.label: Mobility scooter user certification
sections.summary: Only users certified to have relevant medical or physical needs, such as walking difficulties, would be allowed to use mobility scooters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To address this, only users who are certified to have relevant medical or physical needs, such as walking difficulties, would be allowed to use mobility scooters.

sections.label: Regulations effective after 2025 amendments
sections.summary: These regulations will only take effect after legislative amendments are made around 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Lastly, let me emphasise that these regulations will only take effect after legislative amendments are made around 2025.

sections.label: PMA speed and public transport dimensions
sections.summary: The speed limit for PMAs will be reduced to six km/h, and PMAs must comply with public transport dimensions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Second, the speed limit for PMAs will be reduced to six km/h, which is similar to the speed of brisk walking.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Third, to facilitate users to board public transport, PMAs must comply with the dimensions allowed by public transport.

sections.label: Retailers stop new non-compliant PMAs
sections.summary: Retailers can clear existing stock but should stop bringing in new PMAs without a six km/h speed limit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In the meantime, retailers will be able to clear existing stock, but they should stop bringing in new PMAs that do not have a six km/h speed limit.

sections.label: Audio announcements for gracious commuting
sections.summary: New audio announcements were implemented at public transport nodes in 2023 and will be rolled out across about 2,000 buses with speakers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To encourage gracious and caring commuting, new audio announcements have been implemented at public transport nodes in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: They will be rolled out across approximately 2,000 buses that are equipped with speakers from the second quarter of this year.

sections.label: Partners worked with
sections.summary: They have worked with over 100 partners, including schools, social service agencies and corporates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To date, we have worked with over 100 partners, including schools, social service agencies and corporates.

sections.label: Travel Makers programme co-creation
sections.summary: PTC, MINDS, Youth Corps Singapore and SMRT co-created the Travel Makers programme to build confidence in students with intellectual disabilities using public transport independently.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: PTC, MINDS, Youth Corps Singapore (YCS) and SMRT co-created the Travel Makers programme to instill confidence in students with intellectual disabilities to be able to take public transport more independently.

sections.label: Caring Commuters Champions initiative
sections.summary: The Caring Commuters Champions initiative, launched in 2021, aims to train volunteers to better assist fellow commuters in need.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The Caring Commuters Champions initiative, launched in 2021, aims to train volunteers to better assist fellow commuters in need.

sections.label: PMA rules and AMAP recommendations
sections.summary: With AMAP recommendations accepted, PMA rules come into force next year after Active Mobility Act changes, giving three years to adjust; current users need not act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Two years ago, we announced that we are reviewing the use of PMAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: With the acceptance of the AMAP recommendations today, we are saying that the rules will come in force only next year, because the rules need changes to the Active Mobility Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: All in all, there will be three years for users, would-be users and retailers to understand the new rules and to make the changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: For now, users of PMAs, based on current guidelines, need not do anything.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: They do not have to stop using, they do not have to replace their PMAs.

sections.label: Singapore as catch-up port
sections.summary: During COVID-19 supply chain disruptions, Singapore found it can offer itself as a catch-up port for delayed shipping lines to re-organise supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, we saw how supply chains were disrupted and then, along the way, a ship blocked the Suez Canal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We went through a few rounds of this and what we found was that the critical thing that Singapore can play a role in is to offer ourselves as a catch-up port, for shipping lines that were delayed elsewhere, to turn to Singapore as the trusted, reliable port where they could re-organise their supply chains and do some catching up.

sections.label: PMA width and cycling paths
sections.summary: PMAs cannot be wider than 70 centimetres, and the 1,300-kilometre cycling path target can separate different users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, PMAs cannot be wider than 70 centimetres in width.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Where possible, we will look at improving the infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: So, as mentioned, the target of 1,300 kilometres of cycling paths, that would be even more useful as it can separate the different users.

sections.label: Audio announcements on buses
sections.summary: Audio announcements are played at MRT stations and on 2,000 buses with speakers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: On the Member's second question about the audio announcements, we play these at MRT stations and the 2,000 buses with speakers.

sections.label: Bus Captain plays announcement
sections.summary: The Bus Captain plays the audio announcement when a vulnerable commuter boards, and the speaker declares interest as CEO of Strides Premier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: When the Bus Captain sees a vulnerable commuter boarding the bus, that is when the Bus Captain will play the audio announcement, so it will be timely and a reminder to fellow commuters to look out for others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: I want to declare my interest as the CEO of Strides Premier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: We welcome the announcement to extend the lifespan of taxis to 10 years in order to make taxi operations more viable.

sections.label: Taxi lifespan extension discussions
sections.summary: The statutory lifespan extension came about from dialogue and discussions with drivers' associations, operators, taxi drivers and unions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First of all, the extension of the statutory lifespan actually came about because of our dialogue and discussions with the drivers' associations, the operators as well as with the taxi drivers and unions.

sections.label: Passing savings to taxi drivers
sections.summary: The changes aim to reduce operating costs, and savings would as much as possible be passed on to taxi drivers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: These are feedback that have been given and we think that these are changes that we can make quite quickly which will help some way in terms of reducing operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And we are working with the taxi operators to make sure that these savings, barring some increase perhaps in maintenance costs of the older vehicles, as much as possible, would be passed on to the taxi drivers.

sections.label: Making taxi driving attractive
sections.summary: Supply is needed throughout the day, and the aim is to make it more attractive for prospective drivers to take up taxis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And we do need to make sure that there is supply throughout the day.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, we are not looking at levelling the playing field, but we are looking at how to make it more attractive for prospective drivers to decide to take up taxis.

sections.label: PMA rider and cyclist footpath
sections.summary: A PMA rider asked a cyclist to make way, and some Singapore footpaths may not allow two devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Then, I realised what happened after a couple of seconds – the PMA rider was trying to ask the cyclist to make way so that he can get on to that little island before he crossed onto the subsequent zebra crossing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: So, there are footpaths in Singapore that may not be able to allow two devices.

sections.label: Sustainable Aviation Fuel levy on passengers
sections.summary: Singapore is the first country to impose a Sustainable Aviation Fuel levy on passengers, with costs fully loaded on passengers from 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Singapore is the first country in the world to impose a Sustainable Aviation Fuel levy on passengers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: With the cost burden of Sustainable Aviation Fuels fully loaded on passengers from 2026, how can airlines then be incentivised to be fuel-efficient in their operations?

sections.label: Sustainable Aviation Fuel ticket price increases
sections.summary: A 1% Sustainable Aviation Fuel uplift raises economy class tickets by $3 to Bangkok, $6 to Tokyo and $16 to London.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If it is a 1% uplift of Sustainable Aviation Fuel, an economy class ticket to Bangkok will go up by $3; to Tokyo, it will go up by $6; and to London, it will go up by $16.

sections.label: Taxi stands for PHCs and taxis
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked for clarity on taxi stand use by PHCs and taxis, and roll-out conditions and timeline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: In the review of the P2P sector, can the Ministry give clarity on the use of taxi stands for both PHCs and taxis, and what are the roll-out conditions and timeline for this?

sections.label: Taxi stops for PHC pick-up
sections.summary: Taxi stops are for pick-up and drop-off, and allowing PHCs to use them without waiting is being looked into.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Taxi stops are just for pick-up and drop-off.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, one feedback and idea that we are looking into is whether we can allow PHCs to also use the taxi stops to pick up and drop off passengers; no waiting.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Taxi stands, a bit difficult because for PHCs, it is a booking, so, you have to wait for your passenger; unlike taxis where you just queue and then, you just pick up whichever passenger is at the queue and you do not cause congestion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, we will have to talk to the drivers' associations and operators before we can decide.
